summary: Former 1933 airways beacon tower made into a Cibola NF fire lookout; cab replaced 1965; NHLR US 635 (2005); listed standing, not NRHP-eligible in 1988.

facts.design: CL-100 series steel cab, 14 by 14 feet per the 2020 report, on a 10-foot concrete block base
facts.status_note: Latest dated sighting is a 2012 photo caption; the state index lists it standing, but no 2025-26 confirmation was found

events.note: Albuquerque Journal, June 4, 1933: airways beacon tower being made into a fire lookout station; cabin to be built
August 1934 (West Lookouts clipping dated Aug 9, 1934): crew of 15 began work on a ~2.5-mile road from the Oso powerhouse to the lookout; completion not reported
Fire lookout Sam Taylor witnessed a plane crash on Oso Ridge and gave first aid
Register: first lookout was a 25-ft steel tower with wooden cab and ground house; conflicts with the 1933 beacon-tower account
Forest Service placed emergency lookout guards at Oso Ridge and Mount Sedgewick
Mrs. Orby Swatzell on the lookout (Los Cruces Sun-News, July 3, 1944)
William J. Porter on duty (Gallup Independent, May 3, 1947)
Lookout replaced with CL-100 cab on a 10-ft base; register gives cab as 14x4 ft, 2020 report 14x14 ft
Evaluated for NRHP in the Lookouts of the Southwest Region thematic nomination; not eligible due to age
Registered April 1, 2005 as US 635, NM 12; nominated by Dave Lorenz
Photo caption: Oso Ridge fire lookout tower, 2012; latest dated sighting found
2020 FFLA report says the lookout should be re-evaluated and nominated if eligible

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the first 25-ft lookout to 1938; a June 1933 newspaper says an airways beacon tower was being made into a fire lookout. The sources do not say whether these describe the same structure at different stages.
The register gives the 1965 cab as 14 by 4 feet; the 2020 report gives 14 by 14 feet. The design field uses 14 by 14 from the 2020 report; the story states the disagreement.
The register and the 2020 report say concrete block; West Lookouts says cinder block and a storage room.
The register gives 8,713 ft (2,656 m), matching the brief's 2655.7 m; a 1944 newspaper quoted on West Lookouts gives 8,620 ft; a 2011 caption on atchistory gives 9,098 ft.

notes_for_editor: Standing status rests on the undated state index and a 2012 caption; no 2025-26 source found. Access and staffing today are unknown, so no access key. A WebSearch lead (a July 2020 hiker report, about 2.5 miles round trip via NM-53 and Forest Roads 50 and 187) could not be fetched, so it is not used. The register's 14x4 cab figure may be a typo, but the story reports it as stated.
